  WHY: The fragment reaches consumers via `CHANGELOG.md` and says more than §34.B grants, so consumers would expect a cross-repository prevention issue without a §2 ask.

  SEVERITY: NIT

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- CLAUDE.md:1665-1672 (read against §31.B step 2 lines 1480-1486 and step 4 lines 1492-1494) | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: §34.B names only the issue outcome, so a multi-PR prevention fix has no handoff rule: the standing go covers "that issue" which does not exist, and the `/implement-plan-claude` dispatch still needs §23.C approval that neither §34.B nor the §31.B step 3 exception (lines 1487-1491) grants.
  WHY: A session must choose between one issue holding a multi-PR plan (contradicting §31.B step 4) and dispatching without an explicit go (contradicting §23.C), producing a malformed orchestrator issue or an unapproved dispatch.
- changelog.d/9992-claude-md-prevent-recurrence.md:4, 16 | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The fragment still describes the un-narrowed rule: line 4 has no repository limit or PR-review-mode carve-out (§34 intro, CLAUDE.md lines 1633-1635), and line 16 omits the repo-scope restriction it now cites (§23.C, §31.B step 3).
  WHY: The fragment folds verbatim into `CHANGELOG.md`, so consumers would expect a prevention issue in another repository without asking, which §34.B and §23.C forbid, contradicting the entry's §20.E concreteness requirement.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
